title: 2008 Miami Dolphins season
summary:
This document provides a comprehensive overview of the 2008 Miami Dolphins season, which marked a historic turnaround for the franchise. The main points covered include:

**Season Overview**: The document details the Dolphins' remarkable transformation from a 1–15 record in 2007 to an 11–5 record in 2008—the greatest single-season turnaround in NFL history. It was the first season under head coach Tony Sparano, executive vice president Bill Parcells, and general manager Jeff Ireland. The team won the AFC East division title, snapping the New England Patriots' five-year divisional streak, before being eliminated by the Baltimore Ravens in the Wild Card round. The season is also notable for the Dolphins' popularization of the Wildcat offense.

**Offseason Personnel Moves**: This section covers the complete restructuring of the organization, including the hiring of Bill Parcells, dismissal of general manager Randy Mueller, hiring of Jeff Ireland as GM, firing of head coach Cam Cameron, and the search/hiring of Tony Sparano as the eighth head coach in franchise history. It also documents the assembly of Sparano's assistant coaching staff, including coordinators Dan Henning (offense) and Paul Pasqualoni (defense).

**Roster Transactions**: Extensive documentation of player departures (including Zach Thomas and Jason Taylor), re-signings, free agent signings (such as Josh McCown and Justin Smiley), and trades with the Dallas Cowboys (Jason Ferguson, Akin Ayodele, Anthony Fasano) and Washington Redskins (Jason Taylor).

**2008 NFL Draft**: Details on the Dolphins' nine draft selections, headlined by first overall pick Jake Long (offensive tackle from Michigan), along with draft-day trades and subsequent contract signings.

**Preseason and Regular Season**: Coverage of the 3–1 preseason record, week-by-week game summaries (including the Week 3 Wildcat-fueled upset of the Patriots and the Week 17 division-clinching win over the Jets), and detailed in-season transactions.

**Awards and Honors**: Recognition of Tony Sparano as NFL Coach of the Year, Pro Bowl selections Ronnie Brown and Joey Porter, Chad Pennington's NFL Comeback Player of the Year award, and All-Rookie team selections for Jake Long, Kendall Langford, and Dan Carpenter.

**Playoffs**: A summary of the AFC Wild Card loss to the Baltimore Ravens, which ended the Dolphins' season with an 11–6 overall record.
